statement: A 17-week randomized diet trial found that a high-fermented-food diet increased gut microbiome DIVERSITY and decreased 19 inflammatory proteins (including IL-6), while an isolated high-fiber diet did NOT raise diversity and produced person-dependent (microbiome-state-dependent) inflammatory responses.
effect_size: Fermented-food arm: significant rise in microbiota diversity + decrease in 19 inflammatory markers incl. IL-6/IL-10/IL-12b; fiber arm: no diversity change, heterogeneous inflammatory response by baseline microbiome.
population: ~36 healthy adults, randomized to high-fiber vs high-fermented-food, 17 weeks (Stanford)

provenance.primary: Wastyk, Fragiadakis, Perelman, Gardner, Sonnenburg et al. — 'Gut-microbiota-targeted diets modulate human immune status', Cell 2021
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave 4 microbiome deepening → OpenAlex DOI lookup

confidence_notes: Best human RCT here, but: small n, surrogate (diversity + inflammatory proteins) NOT a hard health/aging endpoint, 17 weeks, single site. Counterintuitive fiber null is the honest headline — fiber's benefit appears gated on whether the baseline microbiome can ferment it. Does not show longevity.

statement: Fecal microbiota transfer from young donor mice into aged mice reversed inflammaging signatures in the gut, eye, and brain (and the reciprocal aged-into-young transfer induced them), implicating the aged microbiome as a transmissible contributor to multi-organ inflammaging in this model.
effect_size: Young→aged FMT reduced age-associated intestinal, retinal, and brain inflammation markers; aged→young FMT raised them. Bidirectional transfer design.
population: Young (3mo), old (18mo), aged (24mo) mice, FMT exchange + shotgun metagenomics/metabolomics

provenance.primary: Parker, Romano, Carding et al. — 'Fecal microbiota transfer between young and aged mice reverses hallmarks of the aging gut, eye, and brain', Microbiome 2022
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave 4 — FMT young→old rejuvenation gap (C-domain Wave-2 gap #5)

confidence_notes: Strong CAUSAL hint in mice (intervention, bidirectional) but it is a mouse model of inflammaging markers, not lifespan, and not human. Do not present as evidence the microbiome causes NORMAL human aging.

statement: Recolonizing the gut of middle-aged African turquoise killifish with bacteria from young donors extended lifespan and delayed behavioral decline, the clearest causal demonstration that the gut microbiota can modulate vertebrate lifespan.
effect_size: Young-donor recolonization at middle age extended median/maximal lifespan and preserved young-like microbial diversity and locomotor behavior vs controls.

provenance.primary: Smith, Willemsen, Valenzano et al. — 'Regulation of life span by the gut microbiota in the short-lived African turquoise killifish', eLife 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave 4 — killifish FMT lifespan (named in conflict-microbiome-cause-or-consequence)

confidence_notes: A lifespan (not just marker) effect, but in a uniquely short-lived fish whose rapid aging may exaggerate microbiome leverage. Vertebrate proof-of-principle, not a mammalian or human result.

statement: Akkermansia muciniphila, a mucin-degrading bacterium of the gut mucus layer, is depleted in obese/diabetic mice; administering it (live, or its membrane protein) restored the mucus barrier, reduced metabolic endotoxemia, and reversed diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance.
effect_size: A. muciniphila abundance inversely correlates with body weight; oral administration reversed high-fat-diet metabolic disorders and restored gut barrier (mucus thickness, antimicrobial peptides) in mice.
population: Diet-induced-obese mice; correlative human/rodent abundance data

provenance.primary: Everard, Belzer, Geurts, Cani et al. — 'Cross-talk between Akkermansia muciniphila and intestinal epithelium controls diet-induced obesity', PNAS 2013

confidence_notes: Mechanistically rich mouse work; the basis of Akkermansia's reputation as a 'good' barrier-protective taxon. Mouse metabolic endpoints, not aging or human outcome.

statement: A small exploratory placebo-controlled trial of (pasteurized) Akkermansia muciniphila supplementation in overweight/obese humans was safe and improved insulin sensitivity and several cardiometabolic markers — a proof-of-concept, not a demonstrated clinical or longevity benefit.
effect_size: Pasteurized A. muciniphila improved insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR), insulinemia, plasma total cholesterol, and reduced markers of liver dysfunction/inflammation vs placebo; surrogate endpoints only.
population: n=40 overweight/obese insulin-resistant adults, 3-month exploratory RCT

provenance.primary: Depommier, Everard, Druart, Cani et al. — 'Supplementation with Akkermansia muciniphila in overweight and obese human volunteers: a proof-of-concept exploratory study', Nat Med 2019

confidence_notes: Explicitly labeled exploratory/proof-of-concept (small n, surrogate markers, short). A single probiotic moving HOMA-IR is not a longevity claim. The strongest signal came from the PASTEURIZED (dead) bacterium — a notable wrinkle for the 'live probiotic' narrative.

statement: Commensal-derived butyrate (an SCFA) drives the differentiation of colonic regulatory T cells via histone-deacetylase inhibition at the Foxp3 locus, giving a concrete molecular route from fiber fermentation to immune tolerance / anti-inflammatory tone.
effect_size: Butyrate increased colonic Foxp3+ Treg numbers/function and ameliorated colitis in mice; mechanism = HDAC inhibition enhancing Foxp3 acetylation/expression.
population: Gnotobiotic / SCFA-fed mice; in-vitro T-cell differentiation

provenance.primary: Furusawa, Obata, Fukuda, Ohno et al. — 'Commensal microbe-derived butyrate induces the differentiation of colonic regulatory T cells', Nature 2013

confidence_notes: Solid mechanism in mice; canon-relevant (epigenetic/HDAC link). Mechanism, NOT an outcome — does not by itself show fiber/SCFA extends human healthspan.

statement: Under dietary fiber deprivation, the gut microbiota switches to degrading the host colonic mucus layer as a nutrient source, thinning the protective barrier and increasing susceptibility to enteric pathogens — a mechanistic basis for 'feed your microbes fiber'.
effect_size: Low/zero-fiber diet shifted gnotobiotic community to mucin-degrading taxa, eroded the inner mucus layer, and worsened Citrobacter rodentium infection.
population: Gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined 14-member human microbiota

provenance.primary: Desai, Seekatz, Koropatkin, Martens et al. — 'A Dietary Fiber-Deprived Gut Microbiota Degrades the Colonic Mucus Barrier and Enhances Pathogen Susceptibility', Cell 2016

confidence_notes: Clean mechanism in a defined-community mouse model; does not establish a fiber→longevity outcome in humans. Bridges to the Wastyk fiber-arm null (fiber benefit is microbiome-context-dependent).

statement: The microbiota-accessible-carbohydrate (MAC) hypothesis: the low-fiber industrialized diet starves fiber-fermenting gut microbes, lowering SCFA output and diversity in a way that may compound across generations and contribute to non-communicable 'Western' disease.
effect_size: Framework/review; predicts diversity + SCFA loss under chronic low-MAC intake (later supported in transgenerational mouse work, Sonnenburg 2016).

provenance.primary: Sonnenburg & Sonnenburg — 'Starving our Microbial Self: The Deleterious Consequences of a Diet Deficient in Microbiota-Accessible Carbohydrates', Cell Metabolism 2014

confidence_notes: Influential organizing hypothesis by proponents — frames, does not prove. Graded theoretical. The Wastyk RCT later complicated it (fiber alone did not raise diversity short-term).

statement: The AKEA study used validated record-linkage demography to identify a province of Sardinia (Nuoro/Ogliastra) with an exceptional male-centenarian rate — the original peer-reviewed 'Blue Zone' (the blue pen used to circle the area gave the concept its name).
effect_size: Identified an Extreme Longevity Index hotspot with a near-1:1 male:female centenarian ratio (vs ~1:4-1:5 elsewhere) in inland Sardinia.

provenance.primary: Poulain, Pes, Grasland, Deiana et al. — 'Identification of a geographic area characterized by extreme longevity in the Sardinia island: the AKEA study', Experimental Gerontology 2004

confidence_notes: The DEMOGRAPHIC seed of the Blue Zones idea, and the one with the most age-validation effort. Even so it is a geographic correlation of a longevity statistic — it identifies WHERE, not WHY, and is the cleaner end of a literature whose later popularizations (and some other zones) Newman argues rest on poor age records.

statement: The popular Blue Zones synthesis distilled five long-lived regions (Sardinia, Okinawa, Nicoya, Ikaria, Loma Linda) into nine shared lifestyle 'Power 9' traits — mostly plant-based diet, moderate constant activity, social connection, purpose, moderate alcohol, and stress-down-shifting.
effect_size: 9 cross-region commonalities ('Power 9'); descriptive/observational, no controlled comparison or causal weighting of any single factor.
population: 5 self-selected longevity regions, observational synthesis (National Geographic origin)

provenance.primary: Buettner & Skemp — 'Blue Zones: Lessons From the World's Longest-Lived', American Journal of Lifestyle Medicine 2016

confidence_notes: The Power 9 are biologically plausible and individually echoed by stronger evidence (PREDIMED for diet, social-connection cohorts), BUT as a Blue-Zones inference they are uncontrolled cross-sectional correlations resting on age data Newman shows is unreliable for some zones. Grade the underlying levers on their OWN evidence, not on centenarian counts.

statement: A demographic data-quality analysis (Ig Nobel 2024) argues that extreme-age and 'Blue Zone' longevity records are predicted by markers of error and fraud — late/absent birth registration, poverty, missing death certificates, and pension incentives — rather than by genuine survival, undermining the centenarian-count data the lifestyle inferences rest on.
effect_size: Onset of birth registration coincided with up to ~69-82% drops in apparent supercentenarian rates; remaining hotspots correlate with poverty, old-age, and pension/welfare conditions associated with age misreporting. Preprint/working analysis, contested, not yet a peer-reviewed meta.
population: Cross-national supercentenarian/centenarian records (incl. Blue Zone regions, US, Italy, Japan)

provenance.primary: Saul Justin Newman — 'Supercentenarian and remarkable age records exhibit patterns indicative of clerical errors and pension fraud', bioRxiv 2019 (Ig Nobel Prize in Demography, 2024)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave 4 — DEEPENS D-claims 'blue-zones-data-quality-critique'; the unbiased-grading test case

confidence_notes: DEEPENS (does not duplicate) D's blue-zones-data-quality-critique. Itself graded honestly: a preprint/critique (theoretical tier), high-profile but not consensus-resolved, and disputed by demographers (e.g., GRG/Robine validation work). It does NOT prove Blue-Zone lifestyles are useless — it shows the AGE DATA is unreliable enough that diet/lifestyle claims built on centenarian counts must be graded theoretical/contested, not cohort.
